title: OKR Delivery Charter: Initiative Ownership Ledger, Failure Modes, and Rapid Rebalance Playbook
creator: Alejandro Ruiz
description:
Goal: Create an operational charter that turns company-level OKRs into a single source of truth for initiative ownership, rapid failure detection, and resource rebalancing. This artifact will be used by PMs, ENG leads, Design, and GTM owners to bind quarterly commitments to delivery SLAs and an explicit escalation playbook.

Deliverables:
- Initiative Ownership Ledger (CSV + README) with canonical owners, alternates, success metrics, and scope boundaries.
- Failure Modes Catalog: top 5 ways an initiative can fail (capacity, regressions, cross-team deps, infra SLOs, data quality) with mitigation recipes.
- Rapid Rebalance Playbook: step-by-step decision tree for when to pause/scale/backfill an initiative, with roles and timing (T+24h, T+72h).
- Resource Claim Protocol: lightweight policy for temporary resource shifts between initiatives, including approval path and rollback rules.
- Escalation Triggers + Contact Roster: metrics thresholds, on-call cross-functional contacts, and incident-style postmortem template for OKR misses.
- Acceptance Criteria and Roll-forward Plan template for partial-deliverable shipping and customer-impact minimization.

Context and motivation: Last quarter we observed 3 mid-quarter OKR misses caused by dependency churn and unclear ownership for shared infra pieces. Leadership asked for a practical, field-tested charter that reduces ambiguity, speeds decisions, and preserves customer SLAs. This is scoped to company-level OKRs (top 6 objectives) and their direct initiatives; team-level playbooks remain in each product org.

Stakeholders and review path:
- Primary: PM (Maya Chen), ENG exemplar (Ravi Patel), Design liaison (Sofia Park), Head of GTM (Ibrahim Alami)
- Reviewers: VP Product (Lena Hoffman), CTO (Priya Malhotra), Head of Ops (Jonah Kim)
- Approval: Exec steering committee sign-off required before rollout to cycle leads.

Success metrics (how we will know this shipped successfully):
- 50% reduction in time-to-decision for resource reassignments (baseline measured in Q1 diagnostics).
- 80% of company-level initiatives have an assigned alternate owner in ledger by rollout.
- Fewer than 2 untriaged cross-team blockers per major initiative in the subsequent cycle.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft charter doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/company/okr-delivery-charter (draft)
- Ledger template (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/OKR/ledgers/initiative-ledger-template.csv
- Example postmortem and rollout plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/okr-miss-template
- Related Linear tickets: PM-42188 (initiative gating), ENG-1842 (runtime autoscale work)

Open questions / trade-offs:
1) Ledger ownership model: centralized by PM org vs. federated with sync cadence. Trade-off: centralization reduces duplication but increases friction for small teams. Proposal: central ledger with federated write access + quarterly audit.
2) Strictness of resource claim protocol: lightweight approvals vs. multi-level sign-off. Aim for speed: two-step approval (owner + ops) for claims > 2 FTE-equivalent.
3) Escalation thresholds: metric-based vs. fuzzy. Start metric-based with manual override and continuous refinement.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Week 1: Kickoff, stakeholder interviews, gather examples from last 2 quarters.
- Week 2: Produce ledger template + failure modes catalog; workshop with ENG and Design.
- Week 3: Draft playbook and resource claim flow; simulate 2 past misses against flow.
- Week 4: Executive review, iterate, and finalize.
- Week 5: Rollout to cycle leads and incorporate into cycle planning rituals.

Risks and mitigation:
- Low adoption: mitigate with embedding into planning checklists and required fields in cycle kickoff.
- Overhead for small teams: provide a compact 'light' ledger view and templates.
- Conflicting approvals slowing down critical fixes: allow fast-path emergency approvals with post-hoc audit.

Notes: This ticket will produce both operational artifacts (CSV, templates) and a 1-page executive summary. Post rollout we'll run a light evaluation after the next cycle to measure the stated success metrics.
